newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenyan shilling steadies after weaker opening.
newsitem.headline: Kenyan shilling steadies after weaker opening.

text.p: The shilling firmed against the dollar after a weak opening on Monday, as demand for dollars among offshore investors fell, commercial bank dealers said.
Against the dollar the Central Bank of Kenya posted a mean shilling rate of 57.92 at the opening, compared to 57.37 on Friday. But by Monday afternoon commercial bank rates were posted at 57.85.
Against the pound the shilling was posted at a mean rate of 96.19 from 95.99.

Dealers said the shilling weakened during the last hour of trading on Friday as foreign investors bought dollars, but the shilling was firming on Monday as demand for dollars fell and inflows increased.
Traders were optimistic that the shilling would strengthen in the next few days, although Monday's market had been sluggish.
"A lot will depend on the IMF negotiations. If they go badly then foreign investors could lose faith and come shopping for dollars," one dealer said.

The International Monetary Fund is delaying the release of loans to Kenya and is unhappy with the government over its management of the economy and particularly its handling of a financial scandal that cost the country millions of dollars.
The money market remained liquid. Overnight rates were posted between 10-15 percent unchanged.
But dealers said they expected the market to tighten slightly later in the week as a result of last week's treasury bill auction.
